The amount of time between a correct response and the reinforcement of that response as a significant effect on learning the response. The shorter the time span between a correct response and the reward, the more likely the animal or person will learn that response.

Reinforcement Schedules�

  • Complete reinforcement means that when an animal or person makes a correct response, a reward or reinforcement is given each and every time it occurs. Complete reinforcement is important in the first stages of learning when habits are becoming established.�
  • Partial or intermittent reinforcement means that when an animal or person makes a correct response, sometimes a reward is given, and sometimes it is withheld. Partial reinforcement can follow a definite pattern or sometimes it is random and unpredictable.
    • For example, every third time your dog rolls over on command, you give him a treat.�Or, occasionally you give your dog a biscuit for rolling over on command if you happen to be in a biscuit-giving mood.
